blocks.content: The Director General serves as the apex administrative and operational head of major central organizations, paramilitary forces, and scientific research institutions in India.

headers: Director General of Scientific / Civil Body
rows: Eminent Scientist, Academician, or IAS Officer
Ministry of Home Affairs / State Home Dept.
Respective Administrative Ministry (e.g., Sci & Tech, Health)
Maintenance of Law & Order, Border Security, Counter-Insurgency
Research & Development, Technical Regulation, Policy Execution

items: State DGP appointments must follow the Prakash Singh judgement guidelines, requiring a panel recommendation prepared by the UPSC.
The Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) falls under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and formulates the Exim Policy.
Head of all Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) hold the rank of Director General and report directly to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Director General (DG) is the highest-ranking executive officer in Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) such as BSF, CRPF, CISF, ITBP, and SSB.
In state police administration, the Director General of Police (DGP) serves as the supreme operational commander of the state police force.
Prominent national bodies, including CSIR, ICMR, ICAR, DGCA, and ASI, are also headed by a Director General drawn from civil services or specialized scientific cadres.
Appointments to DG posts in central departments are sanctioned by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) headed by the Prime Minister.
